question: Chariot Disbursements AI overlay at the next re-score: does any Chariot AI capability (the MCP connector, the Gift Processing coding agent, or a newer feature) reach Disbursements? Read the current Chariot help, API reference and changelog for Disbursements; decide whether an agent-capable API without an AI product is an AI component (Endaoment is None (watch) on that basis) and apply one rule to both
conclusion_affected: A2 overlay for Chariot Disbursements (AMBER now; None (watch) with an adjacent-product note under proposed §7a)
rationale: The MCP help page says the connector 'is built for Chariot's Gift Processing platform. It also surfaces DAFpay components'. It does not name Disbursements, so under §7a the v1.1 AMBER for Disbursements has no tied AI component. Two scorers agreed on AMBER, so the downgrade needs adjudication

question: Blackbaud Financial Edge NXT AI status: is the 'Blackbaud Copilot' technical preview in FE NXT (announced 2024-10-07) still live, renamed, or withdrawn? Is any generative-AI feature documented for FE NXT itself in 2025-2026 help or release notes?
conclusion_affected: A1 overlay for Blackbaud FE NXT (AMBER rests on the FE NXT preview; the RE NXT agents are adjacent under proposed §7a)
rationale: The v1.1 basis cites 'AI agents in an adjacent CRM'. Under §7a an adjacent product cannot carry the flag by itself, so FE NXT stays AMBER only if the FE NXT preview, or a successor, is current

question: NCF AI search controls: identify the vendor and model behind ncfgiving.com/ai-search, whether it can read fund or account data, whether queries are logged or used for training, and whether it is linked from the giver portal; set NCF's A1 and A3 overlay at the next re-score

question: Non-AI automation in eligibility screening: harmonise the overlay for automation that is not labelled AI. Morgan Stanley GIFT ('Automated' charity vetting with 'advanced tech') is AMBER (provisional) at v1.2; Givinga ('Automate compliance, charity vetting, and tax documentation') is None evidenced.
